The plan rests Monday and Tuesday. It brings back just two short, gentle walk-runs (20 and 22 min, about 10–12 min of actual running) and adds an easy walk on Sunday. That is a real back-off for an athlete who feels wiped out, and it falls well below her recent volume.

Wednesday is 5 days after the fever ended and her symptoms are above the neck, so a short walk-run is reasonable. Even so, the plan should make Wednesday depend on how she feels. Her own answer (2) says to return once the cough has cleared, but the plan schedules runs while the cough may still be there. That is a small contradiction.

Other small faults: the safety flag says the fever is lingering, but she has had no fever since Friday. The specific dates (Mon Sep 7, Sep 14–20) don't appear in the athlete's card, so they may be invented. The reply also doesn't tie the plan back to the 15 November 5K. It answers her question directly, the plan can be run as written, and it is specific to her illness.

── NESSA'S WEEK ──
Nessa is 41 and new to running, aiming to run the whole Corrowmore Harvest 5K on 15 November without walking. Nessa walk-runs three mornings a week (Monday, Wednesday and Saturday) and walks the dog most days.
Recent weeks: 6.8, 7.3 km
This week: 2.8 km over 1 run. Missed 2 of 3 planned runs.
Body: "Came down with a cold on Tuesday that turned into a fever, 38.4 on Wednesday night. No fever since Friday but still coughing and blocked up."
Feeling: "Wiped out."
Asks: "Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Nessa: Last week you ran once, on Mon Sep 7, and missed the Wednesday and Saturday runs while the cold turned into a fever. …
Answers: (1) No, please do not add the two missed runs, and do not try to run all three days next week (Sep 14 – 20). … (2) Go back to three runs a week, Monday, Wednesday and Saturday, once the cough has cleared and you have had a few good days in a row.
Safety flag: Fever and cough are still lingering
Next week:
Mon: rest. Stay off running while you still have a cough and a blocked nose after a…
Tue: rest. A second rest day lets the cold clear before any running goes back in.
Wed: easy, 20 min walk-run: 5 min walk, then 5 rounds of 2 min run and 1 min walk, heart…
Thu: rest. Keeps the gap between the two short runs.
Fri: rest. Last full rest day before the weekend run, so the body can absorb the first…
Sat: easy, 22 min walk-run: 4 min walk, then 6 rounds of 2 min run and 1 min walk, heart…
Sun: other, 30 min walk at an easy pace. Walking keeps you moving while the cold clears…
